rationale: Ground truth has no substantive concerns (bot rate-limited, humans just said thanks), so recall is vacuous for both. Both candidates independently converge on the two real gaps beyond the diff's headline fix — missing pytestmark causing the new test to be deselected in CI, and warmup_quack_fp8() bypassing the new gate — which is a strong cross-validation signal that these are grounded. X presents this with concrete verification (actual pytest collect-only output showing '18 deselected'), clean prioritization (Blocking/Should-fix/Minor/Question), and precise suggested diffs, making every finding immediately actionable. Y covers similar ground but buries it under redundant templated 'Validated/claim-verified/resolved' bullets that mostly restate the same facts, and two of its findings cite broken locations ('?:102', '?:33') instead of real file paths, hurting both precision and actionability. X's speculative items (sticky-disable, warning_once dedup) are clearly hedged as design suggestions rather than confirmed defects, whereas Y's noisier format makes it harder to distinguish verified fact from speculation.
